# FlashForge AD5M Klipper fork vs upstream v0.11.0

**Date:** 2026-06-04
**Status:** evidence-backed, generated by direct file-level diff
**Inputs:**
  - upstream: `Klipper3d/klipper @ v0.11.0` (`e02b725602067a2cd098a62be9a4bb10fc74a9bd`, 2022-11-29)
  - fork: `FlashForge/AD5M_Series_Klipper @ 6f479ea` (HEAD, 2024-05-09; only 4 commits total, code unchanged since `6c925c5` "first commit" 2024-01-24)
**See also:** [`../reverse-engineering/ad5m-mcu-firmware-and-config.md`](../reverse-engineering/ad5m-mcu-firmware-and-config.md), [`../../br-external/package/klipper/klipper.mk`](../../br-external/package/klipper/klipper.mk)

---

## 1. TL;DR

The FlashForge fork is **six small file changes** on top of stock `Klipper3d/klipper v0.11.0`. The MCU firmware sources (`src/`) are byte-identical to upstream. The fork additionally bundles two prebuilt MCU binaries that ship in the AD5M factory image.

ReForge pins **upstream v0.11.0** (`e02b725602067a2cd098a62be9a4bb10fc74a9bd`) and carries **six patches**:

1. `0001-chelper-disable-runtime-build-check.patch` — the chelper runtime-build-check disable, matching the FF fork's change exactly (see §2.1).
2. `0002-py3-configfile-read_file.patch` — **Python 3.12+ blocker.** v0.11.0 calls `fileconfig.readfp()` which was removed in Python 3.12. We ship Python 3.14, so klippy aborts at first config load without this patch. Backport of upstream Klipper PR [#6388](https://github.com/Klipper3d/klipper/pull/6388); the change landed on master at `klippy/configfile.py:165-169`.
3. `0003-py3-gcode-regex-raw-string.patch` — **Python 3.14 blocker.** v0.11.0's `klippy/gcode.py:396` uses `re.compile('^(?:[nN][0-9]+)?\s*[mM]112(?:\s|$)')` — an unrecognised string escape in a non-raw string. Python 3.6–3.11 silently accepted it, 3.12–3.13 emitted a `SyntaxWarning`, **3.14 raised it to `SyntaxError`** so the module fails to import. The FlashForge fork has the same bug. Matches master's `gcode.py:432` (raw-string prefix).
4. `0004-toolhead-backport-lookahead-flush-time.patch` — **upstream backport** of commit `16fc46fe5` (Kevin O'Connor, 2025-09-30): `LOOKAHEAD_FLUSH_TIME` 0.250 → 0.150. Reduces "print stall" corner cases (which is what forge-x's `fix_enable_e17` workaround addresses on this exact hardware). Upstream took this change for general responsiveness; forge-x users have been running the same value for months. Low-risk one-line change.
5. `0005-relax-TRSYNC_TIMEOUT-ffad5m.patch` — doubles MCU sync ack window from 25 ms (`TRSYNC_TIMEOUT = 0.025`) to 50 ms (`0.05`). Preempts the sporadic E0011 "MCU communication timeout" shutdowns observed across the AD5M user base on forge-x. Same value forge-x ships as `fix_enable_e11`; promoted from `disabled-patches/` to default-applied on 2026-06-05 based on field evidence (forge-x's broad user base on the same hardware class) rather than waiting to observe E0011 on our specific test unit. Upstream Klipper master still ships `0.025`; no upstream PR thread.
6. `0006-stepcompress-bump-queue-start-size.patch` — matches the FlashForge fork's `QUEUE_START_SIZE 1024 → 2048` in `klippy/chelper/stepcompress.c`. Saves one realloc-and-memcpy per stepper queue at the cost of allocating twice as many initial slots upfront (~5–10 KB total across the AD5M's 5 steppers; trivial). Upstream still ships `1024` on v0.11.0, v0.12.0 and master; FlashForge picked `2048` at first fork commit and has shipped it across the entire AD5M user base since 2024-01.

The other 5 fork deltas are catalogued below and intentionally not carried; any can be re-applied as a patch later if it turns out to matter on hardware.

## Forge-x tunings reviewed for default-adoption (2026-06-05)

See `forge-x/.shell/commands/ztune_klipper.sh`, `forge-x/tuning.cfg`, and `forge-x/.py/klipper/patches/`. Decision matrix:

| forge-x lever | what it does | upstream status | our decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| `LOOKAHEAD_FLUSH_TIME = 0.150` (toolhead.py) | flush lookahead queue ~6–7 ×/s instead of ~4 ×/s | **adopted by upstream master in 2025-09 (commit 16fc46fe5)** | **carried as patch 0004 by default** |
| `TRSYNC_TIMEOUT = 0.05` (mcu.py) | doubles the MCU sync-ack window 25 ms → 50 ms; fixes spurious E0011 on this hardware | not adopted by upstream | **carried as patch 0005 by default** (2026-06-05) — forge-x's user-base evidence on the same hardware is strong enough; preemptive default. |
| `[klippy] log_config: False` | skips the full-config dump that klippy writes to `klippy.log` on every restart (~5–10 KB) | not in upstream (forge-x adds the gate via a 1-line patch to `configfile.py`) | **not carried** — marginal log/memory hygiene; not worth a custom patch |
| `[statistics] disabled: True` | suppresses the 1-line-per-second `Stats <time>: sysload=... cputime=... memavail=...` log lines from `klippy/extras/statistics.py` | not in upstream (forge-x adds the gate via a patch to `statistics.py`) | **not carried** — marginal log-noise reduction; doesn't free CPU since callbacks still run |
| `[stepper_{x,y}] rotation_distance: 39.9` | tunes belt step ratio off the nominal 40.0 by 0.25% | n/a — user calibration | **not carried** — each user must calibrate their own printer; our default mirrors the factory config |
| `[stepper_z] rotation_distance: 7.98` | tunes Z leadscrew similarly off-nominal | n/a — user calibration | **not carried** (same reason) |
| `[extruder] rotation_distance: 4.4` | the forge-x author's specific extruder calibration | n/a — user calibration | **not carried** — we keep the factory's 4.7 (ZMod ships the same); user must `EXTRUDE_TEST` and tune |
| `[probe] speed: 2 lift_speed: 5 samples: 2` | aggressive probe-tuning preferences | n/a — user preference | **not carried** |
| `[printer] square_corner_velocity: 9` | corner-velocity preference (default is 5) | n/a — user preference | **not carried** |
| `[stepper_z] second_homing_speed: 2` | slow precise second-homing | n/a — user preference | **not carried** — reasonable, but per-user |
| zram VM sysctls (swappiness=100, page-cluster=0, etc.) | tunes the VM for zram-as-primary-swap | n/a — system tuning | **already shipped** (`.shell/reforge-vmtune.sh`, sourced by `S35zram`) |
| jemalloc preload + `MALLOC_CONF=narenas:1,...` | per-process allocator tuning | n/a — system tuning | **already shipped + extended** (our autoresearch added `tcache:false` on top, see `autoresearch.md`) |

## 2. Verbatim file-level diff (code only)

Six files differ. Diffs reproduced exactly.

### 2.1 `klippy/chelper/__init__.py` — runtime build check disabled

```diff
@@ -266,13 +266,13 @@
         srcfiles = get_abs_files(srcdir, SOURCE_FILES)
         ofiles = get_abs_files(srcdir, OTHER_FILES)
         destlib = get_abs_files(srcdir, [DEST_LIB])[0]
-        if check_build_code(srcfiles+ofiles+[__file__], destlib):
-            if check_gcc_option(SSE_FLAGS):
-                cmd = "%s %s %s" % (GCC_CMD, SSE_FLAGS, COMPILE_ARGS)
-            else:
-                cmd = "%s %s" % (GCC_CMD, COMPILE_ARGS)
-            logging.info("Building C code module %s", DEST_LIB)
-            do_build_code(cmd % (destlib, ' '.join(srcfiles)))
+       # if check_build_code(srcfiles+ofiles+[__file__], destlib):
+       #     if check_gcc_option(SSE_FLAGS):
+       #         cmd = "%s %s %s" % (GCC_CMD, SSE_FLAGS, COMPILE_ARGS)
+       #     else:
+       #         cmd = "%s %s" % (GCC_CMD, COMPILE_ARGS)
+       #     logging.info("Building C code module %s", DEST_LIB)
+       #     do_build_code(cmd % (destlib, ' '.join(srcfiles)))
         FFI_main = cffi.FFI()
```

**Why FF did it:** target has no gcc; can't rebuild `c_helper.so` at runtime.

**ReForge stance: carried as `0001-chelper-disable-runtime-build-check.patch`.** We cross-compile `c_helper.so` at Buildroot time (see `KLIPPER_BUILD_CMDS` in `klipper.mk`) and the install ordering already leaves the `.so` strictly newer than every source, so the runtime mtime check returns False even without the patch (empirically verified, 2026-06-04). The patch is defensive insurance against any future post-install hook, OTA script, or `find -exec touch` flow that re-touches a chelper source after the `.so` install — the adversarial test (`touch stepcompress.c` after install) confirmed `check_build_code` flips to True in that case, which would cause klippy to invoke gcc and abort startup on the target.

### 2.2 `klippy/chelper/stepcompress.c` — bigger initial step queue

```diff
-#define QUEUE_START_SIZE 1024
+#define QUEUE_START_SIZE 2048
```

**Why FF did it:** larger initial allocation → fewer realloc events on long moves; pure perf tuning, no behavioral change.

**ReForge stance: carried as `0006-stepcompress-bump-queue-start-size.patch` (2026-06-05).** Matches the FF fork value. Cost is trivial (~5–10 KB upfront across the AD5M's 5 steppers); benefit is one fewer realloc-and-memcpy per stepper queue at startup. Same field-evidence rationale as 0005.

### 2.3 `klippy/extras/tmc.py` — TMC echeck-reset suppressed

```diff
-            did_reset = self.echeck_helper.start_checks()
-            if did_reset:
-                self.mcu_phase_offset = None
+            #did_reset = self.echeck_helper.start_checks()
+            #if did_reset:
+            #    self.mcu_phase_offset = None
```

**Why FF did it:** suppresses spurious phase-offset resets when the TMC error check fires during operation.

**ReForge risk if we don't carry it:** during a print, if a TMC driver hits an error condition (overtemp, short), the start_checks() pass may reset `mcu_phase_offset`, which causes the next stepper move to recalibrate phase. On the AD5M's TMC drivers (which FlashForge tuned around for some unknown reason) this apparently mis-fires. **Not carrying** until we observe the failure mode on hardware.

### 2.4 `klippy/extras/virtual_sdcard.py` — `.gx` extension + UTF-8 tolerance

```diff
-VALID_GCODE_EXTS = ['gcode', 'g', 'gco']
+VALID_GCODE_EXTS = ['gcode', 'g', 'gco','gx']
@@
-            if fname not in flist:
-                fname = files_by_lower[fname.lower()]
+            #if fname not in flist:
+                #fname = files_by_lower[fname.lower()]
             fname = os.path.join(self.sdcard_dirname, fname)
-            f = io.open(fname, 'r', newline='')
+            f = io.open(fname, 'r', errors='ignore', newline='')
```

**Why FF did it:** FlashForge's OrcaSlicer fork emits `.gx` files; non-UTF-8 bytes (embedded thumbnails or BOMs) blow up the default decoder; case-insensitive lookup masks slicer/UI casing bugs.

**ReForge stance:** the `.gx` extension matters for FF-slicer users. We may re-add this as a small patch once we hit a `.gx` file in testing. The `errors='ignore'` is benign and worth carrying. The case-insensitive disable seems wrong — it's a regression hiding upstream's fallback. Skip that one.

### 2.5 `klippy/mcu.py` — diagnostic log line

```diff
@@ -742,6 +742,11 @@
             self._send_config(config_params['crc'])
         # Setup steppersync with the move_count returned by get_config
         move_count = config_params['move_count']
+        move_msg = "My Configured MCU '%s' (%d moves)" % (self._name, move_count)
+        logging.info(move_msg)
+        log_info = self._log_info() + "\n" + move_msg
+        self._printer.set_rollover_info(self._name, log_info, log=False)
+
         if move_count < self._reserved_move_slots:
             raise error("Too few moves available on MCU '%s'" % (self._name,))
```

Pure debug logging. No behavioral effect. Skip.

### 2.6 `klippy/queuelogger.py` — log rotation tuning

```diff
-            self, filename, when='midnight', backupCount=5)
+            self, filename, when='h', interval=4, backupCount=6)
```

Rotate every 4h × 6 backups instead of nightly × 5. FF-internal field-support preference. Skip.

## 3. Files identical to upstream v0.11.0

- **All of `src/`** (the MCU firmware C sources) — every `.c` and `.h` is a byte-for-byte match. The `Mainboard-20230831.bin` and `Eboard-20231012.hex` shipped in `fw-Ad5m/` (and in stock OTA `control-2.2.3.tar.xz`) were built from this unmodified source tree with the FF board Kconfig selections.
- **`klippy/extras/adxl345.py`** — both fork and upstream v0.11.0 use:
  ```python
  mcu.add_config_cmd("query_adxl345 oid=%d clock=0 rest_ticks=0" % (oid,), on_restart=True)
  ...
  self.query_adxl345_cmd = self.mcu.lookup_command("query_adxl345 oid=%c clock=%u rest_ticks=%u", cq=cmdqueue)
  ```
- **`src/sensor_adxl345.c`** — both fork and upstream v0.11.0 declare:
  ```c
  DECL_COMMAND(command_query_adxl345, "query_adxl345 oid=%c clock=%u rest_ticks=%u");
  ```
  → the `clock=%u rest_ticks=%u` format has been the protocol since v0.11.0. The earlier ReForge note in `docs/reverse-engineering/ad5m-mcu-firmware-and-config.md` claiming "v11 MCU: `query_adxl345 oid=%c rest_ticks=%u` (no `clock`)" was **wrong** — that format is v0.10 era. A v0.11 host against a v0.11 MCU has no skew on `query_adxl345`. Correction filed alongside this note.

## 5. Decision (2026-06-04)

- **Pin upstream `Klipper3d/klipper @ v0.11.0`** (`e02b725602067a2cd098a62be9a4bb10fc74a9bd`).
- **Carry one patch:** `0001-chelper-disable-runtime-build-check.patch` (matches FF fork's change exactly; defensive guard against future flows that could re-touch chelper sources after the `.so` install).
- **Parked, not applied:** `0002-relax-TRSYNC_TIMEOUT-ffad5m.patch` lives under `br-external/package/klipper/disabled-patches/` so Buildroot ignores it (the patch glob is package-root-only). Move it back up to re-enable. See that directory's `README.md` for the re-enable trigger (E0011 communication-timeout shutdowns observed on hardware).
- **Use the verbatim factory `printer.cfg` + `printer.base.cfg`** from `reference/ad5m-factory-config/` (extracted from the 3.1.3 factory image). The earlier ReForge-banner-and-comment-decorated copies are gone.

**Known risks of the patches we DON'T currently apply:**

1. *Parked `0002` TRSYNC_TIMEOUT bump.* forge-x raised it from 25 ms to 50 ms to silence E0011 communication-timeout shutdowns on this exact platform. If E0011s show up during printing on the live trial, move `disabled-patches/0002-relax-TRSYNC_TIMEOUT-ffad5m.patch` back up to the package root.
2. *No `.gx` slicer extension* in `virtual_sdcard.VALID_GCODE_EXTS`. FF-slicer users will see "unknown gcode extension" until we add it.
3. *No TMC echeck-reset suppression.* If TMC drivers throw spurious phase-offset resets on the AD5M (FF apparently tuned around this), we'll see them. Re-add `klippy/extras/tmc.py` echeck comment-out if observed.

Each is a small, isolated patch that we can re-introduce on demand. Carrying them upfront before observing the failure mode adds maintenance burden and obscures provenance.

## 6. How this diff was generated (reproducer)

```sh
git clone --depth 200 --branch v0.11.0 https://github.com/Klipper3d/klipper /tmp/upstream
git clone https://github.com/FlashForge/AD5M_Series_Klipper /tmp/fork
diff -rq /tmp/upstream/klippy /tmp/fork/klippy | grep -vE '__pycache__|\.pyc$|c_helper\.so'
diff -rq /tmp/upstream/src   /tmp/fork/src     # expect: zero output
```
